source_specific_acceptance_reasoning: The prior card correctly identified the central bounded contribution: a natural-language specification is transformed into a hybrid pseudo-program plus task-conditioned PEFT artifact for a frozen lightweight interpreter, and the paper reports substantial exact-match and local-runtime results. It nevertheless contains material factual and semantic errors that cannot receive an ACCEPT or NARROW verdict. FuzzyBench-10M is described as synthetic and released, not proprietary; the currently public verified dataset is only a 50,678-example test/test_clean subset, so the precise boundary is incomplete public release of the claimed 10M corpus. The paper does not define probabilistic semantics or state that correctness is probabilistic. Its empirical exact-match tests, robustness perturbations and ablations are bounded Validator evidence even though they are neither formal verification nor empirical validation of the ignition architecture. Case studies compose PAW calls with keyword search, regex and deterministic Python in user code, but no learned program-composition algebra, adapter arithmetic or formal router is supplied. The paper supports a versioned distributable artifact concept; current SDKs additionally implement slugs, immutable pinned versions and caches, but those current service features must not be projected backward as a governed paper-era provenance registry. The corrected card therefore remains PARTIAL while superseding the prior card for downstream synthesis.
accepted_prior_claims: PAW defines a hybrid discrete pseudo-program plus continuous PEFT artifact executed by a frozen interpreter.
The main text reports a Qwen3-4B compiler, frozen Qwen3-0.6B interpreter, rank-64 LoRA with 64 shared bases, and FuzzyBench-10M spanning more than 800 task categories.
The paper reports 73.78 exact match for the final 0.6B PAW system versus 68.70 for direct Qwen3-32B prompting, subject to synthetic-benchmark and system-comparability limits.
The compiler/interpreter split and reusable single-file artifact are concrete evidence for Function OS representation, compiler, artifact and interpreter nodes.
The paper provides no formal specification language, semantic-equivalence checker, effect calculus or formal correctness guarantee.

material_corrections.corrected: Bounded empirical Validator evidence exists through exact-match benchmarks, controlled ablations, noisy-specification tests, local runtime checks and small deployed case studies; this is not formal verification, architecture proof or empirical validation of Function OS.

specification_language: Unstructured natural-language function descriptions, optionally with examples and constraints, transformed by a pseudo compiler into a restatement-plus-examples token sequence. There is no typed contract, formal pre/postcondition language or machine-checked specification semantics.
uncertainty_model: No calibrated uncertainty, confidence, abstention, repeated-run dispersion or probabilistic semantics is supplied. Main results are predominantly point estimates on synthetic data; the verified subset uses agreement between gpt-5.2 and gpt-5-mini as a label-quality filter, not a PAW uncertainty model. Robustness scores under perturbed specifications are sensitivity evidence only.
lifecycle_and_provenance: The paper presents a reusable single-file artifact that can be named, versioned, cached and distributed, but it does not give an immutable build receipt, dataset manifest, compiler/interpreter compatibility contract, signed provenance, rollback protocol or governed registry schema. Current public Python/JS SDKs add versioned slugs, immutable pinned versions and caching; current compiler and verified-test artifacts are public snapshots, but the compiler model card lacks a declared license and the full 10M training split was not located.
composition_rule: Only external sequential/orchestrated composition in ordinary user code is demonstrated. The 10-function tool-calling pipeline delegates time parsing to regex and JSON assembly to deterministic Python; the reranking case combines a keyword index with a PAW reranker. No algebra over LoRA artifacts, merge safety, associativity, routing contract or learned multi-step composition is validated.
state_or_effect_model: The paper models a per-call autoregressive fuzzy function and does not define persistent state, external effects, effect types, transactional behavior or effect routing. Autoregressive token state within a call must not be conflated with a Function OS state/effect model.
validation_regime: Empirical exact-match evaluation on synthetic FuzzyBench splits, six small image tasks, component ablations, noisy-specification perturbations, a 4,096-example quantization subset, two 36-example compact-model sets and case studies. No formal proof, architecture-level empirical validation, equivalence certificate, independent replication, repeated-run uncertainty or comprehensive external-domain validation is established.
equivalence_notions: Exact string match to synthetic references is the principal task metric. It is not semantic equivalence between specifications, generated artifacts, PEFT methods, compiler versions or a symbolic reference implementation.

source_specific_acceptance_reasoning: The prior review correctly captured the central bounded result: the numerator and normalization state of causal linear attention can be written as an incrementally programmed fast-weight associative memory, and a learned delta-style update provides an explicit state-dependent write instruction. Material corrections are nevertheless required. The exact registered bytes are arXiv v3, not v1. Capacity is bounded by the feature-space dimension d_dot under an orthogonality/interference argument, not generically by the raw matrix dimension; DPFP changes d_dot and the empirical threshold is approximate. There is no standalone compiler or persistent program artifact: slow learned projections produce keys, values and write strengths online inside a layer, W and z are ephemeral recurrent state, and queries read that state. The paper's stochastic training and FAVOR+ random features do not make the fast-weight function semantically probabilistic; DPFP is expressly deterministic. Empirical results support the proposed update relative to matched sum-update linear baselines, but DPFP does not beat the standard Transformer or the largest Performer configuration on WMT14, Delta Net remains worse than the standard Transformer in the limited-context WikiText table, and it trails Transformer-XL with sufficiently larger state in the untruncated comparison. The official synthetic repository supplies source and 320 CSV logs, but the driver effectively uses one fixed seed because the parsed --seed value is not passed to run, reports best validation values without dispersion, and regenerates FAVOR+ Omega on every forward call even in evaluation although the paper says evaluation features are fixed. The separate language-model repository has code but no tracked tests, result logs or checkpoints, and no pinned translation port was found. The corrected record therefore remains PARTIAL and supersedes the prior card for synthesis.
accepted_prior_claims: Causal linear attention admits a concrete fast-weight representation W plus normalization accumulator z, updated by outer products and read by a query.
The delta instruction reads the current value at a key, learns a sigmoid write strength beta and updates W by beta times the value error outer-product the key feature.
The paper gives a bounded orthogonality/interference capacity argument and tests it on synthetic associative retrieval.
DPFP is a deterministic parameter-free feature map intended to increase projected dimension and encourage sparse, more orthogonal keys.
Mutable fast-weight memory is explicit within sequence processing, while no typed effect system, persistent artifact registry or program-equivalence checker is provided.

material_corrections.prior: preprint v1
material_corrections.corrected: The exact frozen hash/size bytes and arXiv API identify arXiv:2102.11174v3; the 16 pages combine the 12-page PMLR paper and 4-page supplement.

material_corrections.prior: Linear self-attention mechanisms are formally equivalent to FWPs.
material_corrections.corrected: The paper rewrites causal linearised attention's core numerator as an outer-product fast-weight memory and includes accumulator z for normalization. This is a mechanism-level algebraic correspondence, not an equivalence of whole Transformers, trained programs or observable semantics.

material_corrections.prior: Capacity is bounded by matrix dimension d.
material_corrections.corrected: The interference argument uses at most d_dot mutually orthogonal key features; d_dot depends on phi and equals 2*d_key*nu for DPFP. It is an idealized upper-bound argument with approximate empirical thresholds, not a universal exact capacity theorem for trained sequence models.

material_corrections.prior: The matrix is overwritten at each step.
material_corrections.corrected: Additive linear attention accumulates outer products. The proposed delta state transition selectively removes and writes the association along the current key; it does not replace the entire matrix.

material_corrections.prior: Self-attention is a concrete compiler and W dot q is a separately executed interpreter.
material_corrections.corrected: This is a useful architectural analogy only: learned slow projections generate online write/read vectors inside one causal layer, not an offline compiler producing a persistent deployable artifact for an independent interpreter.

material_corrections.prior: The FWP learns by gradient descent and its behavior is probabilistic.
material_corrections.corrected: Training is stochastic and FAVOR+ introduces output variance through sampled features, but the paper supplies no probabilistic program semantics. The proposed DPFP path is deterministic given parameters and inputs.

material_corrections.prior: Translation and language-model experiments show competitive or improved performance compared with standard linear attention.
material_corrections.corrected: Delta updates consistently improve matched sum-update linear baselines in reported WikiText settings. DPFP improves small-d_dot linear alternatives on WMT14 but scores 27.1 test versus 27.7 for both the standard Transformer and the largest Performer; Delta Net is 31.5 versus standard Transformer 29.6 in the medium limited-context table and 29.4 versus Transformer-XL 25.5 when the latter uses much larger state.

material_corrections.prior: No Validator evidence because validation is not formal.
material_corrections.corrected: Equation-level identities, synthetic capacity/update tests, WMT/WikiText evaluations and ablations are bounded behavioral-check evidence. They are not an architecture proof, semantic-equivalence service or empirical validation of Function OS; source receipts are incomplete and no independent reproduction was performed.

specification_language: No external function-specification language is defined. The input sequence induces online keys, values, queries and write strengths through trained projections; training objectives rather than contracts specify useful behavior.
uncertainty_model: No calibrated predictive uncertainty, acceptance threshold or repeated-run dispersion is reported. Synthetic figures use the best validation loss per model/size; the released driver defaults effectively to one seed and evaluates 20 sampled sequences. FAVOR+ samples random feature matrices and the paper notes output variance, whereas DPFP is deterministic. These facts do not amount to probabilistic program semantics.
lifecycle_and_provenance: The programmed W and z are per-sequence runtime state, initialized to zero and normally not persisted or versioned. The paper-linked MIT synthetic repository is a ten-commit, untagged snapshot with 320 CSV logs but no tests/checkpoints; its --seed argument is not propagated and its FAVOR+ evaluation implementation does not visibly fix Omega. The Apache language-model repository's current head postdates the paper and contains scripts/source but no tests, results or checkpoints. The described FAIRSEQ translation port is not pinned in the linked assets. No artifact identity, compatibility manifest, signed provenance, migration or rollback contract exists.
composition_rule: Programming instructions compose sequentially as state transitions over W and z. Additive updates sum outer products; delta updates are state-dependent and beta-gated. This is within-layer temporal accumulation/update, not composition of independently specified function artifacts and not a multi-function router.
state_or_effect_model: W and normalization accumulator z are explicit mutable mathematical state. They are reset to zero per sequence in the derivation; the untruncated-language-model experiment carries fast-weight memory across training segments while truncating backpropagation. No external effects, effect typing, transactions, isolation or persistence contract is defined.
validation_regime: Algebraic mechanism derivations; two synthetic associative-retrieval settings; WMT14 BLEU; WikiText-103 perplexity in limited, non-overcapacity and carried-context configurations; normalization/position/state-size ablations; throughput and memory point measurements. Main results lack multi-seed dispersion/significance. Reported failure boundaries include attention-normalization accumulator growth, divergence without sum normalization in some runs, worse-than-standard baselines, FAVOR+ plus delta NaNs in an appendix setting and finite-capacity interference.
equivalence_notions: Equations 8-19 establish a bounded computational correspondence between causal linearised attention and normalized outer-product fast-weight updates. Appendix B compares two update rules under orthogonal-key assumptions and shows preservation of an unrelated association for the proposed rule. Neither result provides behavioral equivalence between trained models, specifications, checkpoints or implementations.

source_specific_acceptance_reasoning: The prior card correctly identifies NFTs as attention-based neural functionals that operate directly on structured neural-network parameters while respecting bounded neuron-permutation symmetries, and correctly retains only PARTIAL Function OS support. It cannot be accepted unchanged. Its recorded hash, zero-byte size and ANCHOR_VERIFIED status do not describe the registered artifact. The carrier is a tuple of layer weight and bias tensors with coupled row/column actions and layer identity, not a flat vector. Hidden-neuron permutations preserve the represented function when coupled across adjacent layers, but the paper's full S_NP group also permutes input and output indices, an assumption the authors call usually too strong and mitigate with learned I/O position encodings. Theorem 3.1 proves minimal equivariance of the constructed layer class relative to that defined group and excludes arbitrary entry-wise false symmetries; it is not a general behavioral-equivalence checker. Full attention is normally intractable at O(dim(W)^2 c), so the implementation uses row-column-sum attention with stated O(L^2 c) attention plus O(L n^3 c) equivariant terms. NFTs are neural functionals that consume and may modify weights; standard inference evaluates the NFT itself and does not interpret the input network's original input-output function. INR2Array composes an invariant NFT encoder with a latent array and hypernetwork decoder, then freezes the encoder for a Transformer classifier. The table reports CIFAR INR2Array NFT 63.4 plus-or-minus 0.00 versus NFN 46.6 plus-or-minus 0.13, while prose says 64.4, a one-point internal contradiction; vanilla NFT classification is 44.8 and does not beat NFN. Accuracy-prediction NFTs slightly beat NFNP but not NFNHNP. Experiments are bounded behavioral checks, not formal verification, proof of downstream correctness or empirical validation of Function OS. The current official source has runnable structure and one randomized equivariance/sensitivity test module, but no immutable datasets, result logs, checkpoints, fixed experiment receipts or visible global use of configured seeds; tests were not executed because the local environment lacks PyTorch. The corrected record remains PARTIAL and supersedes the prior card for synthesis.
accepted_prior_claims: NFTs use attention to process neural-network weight spaces and are constructed to respect defined neuron-permutation actions.
The architecture includes equivariant self-attention, invariant learned-query cross-attention and deep blocks built from attention, pointwise nonlinearities and equivariant linear layers.
INR2Array uses an NFT encoder to produce a fixed latent array and a hypernetwork decoder to reconstruct a SIREN, after which the frozen encoder supports classification.
The paper evaluates CNN accuracy prediction, SIREN classification and SIREN editing, and explicitly reports compute and training-stability limitations.
No typed specification language, effect calculus, general equivalence service, composition algebra or processed-artifact registry is supplied.

material_corrections.prior: SHA-256 0582e5..., size 0 and ANCHOR_VERIFIED.
material_corrections.corrected: The exact registered conference PDF is SHA-256 958c0c85053228dc8d7a61bec74a09da327de0772b84e769e3d7c10b1d1a370e, 2,924,528 bytes and 18 pages; the anchor manifest says EXTRACTED_NOT_ANCHOR_VERIFIED. Codex independently reviewed full text and every page.

material_corrections.prior: Neural network weights as flat vectors with permutation structure.
material_corrections.corrected: The paper represents an L-layer network as structured layer tensors, with biases and optional feature channels; permutations act through coupled rows and columns while preserving layer boundaries. Flattening is neither the formal carrier nor the implementation interface.

material_corrections.prior: Neuron permutation symmetries exactly preserve behavior, without qualification.
material_corrections.corrected: Coupled hidden-neuron permutations preserve the represented function. The paper's S_NP additionally permits input/output permutations, which the authors say is usually too strong; learned I/O positional encodings remove that unwanted equivariance in practice. Theorem 3.1 is an architectural minimal-equivariance result, not general semantic equivalence.

material_corrections.prior: The NFT architecture itself is the interpreter for the input function.
material_corrections.corrected: An NFT is a learned neural functional over parameters. Standard inference executes the NFT mapping; it does not execute or interpret the processed network on that network's input domain.

material_corrections.prior: NFTs match or exceed prior methods and INR2Array improves classification by up to plus 17 percent.
material_corrections.corrected: The plus 16.8-point CIFAR improvement is for INR2Array with an NFT encoder relative to the previous NFN result. Vanilla NFT classification is lower than NFN; accuracy prediction does not beat the best HNP baseline. The paper also contradicts itself with 63.4 in tables versus 64.4 in prose.

material_corrections.prior: Predicting test accuracy is empirical validation.
material_corrections.corrected: The symmetry proof, prediction metrics, classification/editing results and ablations are bounded theorem-and-behavioral-check evidence. They are not formal verification of outputs, independent reproduction, architecture proof or empirical validation of Function OS; current source lacks immutable run receipts.

specification_language: No external function-specification language is defined. NFT behavior is selected by architecture, learned parameters and task loss. Tensor-shape/layer specifications constrain supported input networks, but they are implementation contracts rather than semantic pre/postconditions.
uncertainty_model: No calibrated predictive uncertainty, abstention rule or probabilistic/fuzzy semantics is defined. Reported standard errors cover three runs for classification/editing and two runs for generalization as stated in the appendix, but CIFAR INR2Array entries round to plus-or-minus 0.00 and the released drivers do not visibly consume configured seeds globally. Dispersion reporting is evaluation metadata, not a semantic uncertainty model.
lifecycle_and_provenance: Inputs are static parameter snapshots or paper-linked SIREN datasets. The current MIT repository and PyPI 0.1.2 package provide code identity and packaging, but the repository has no tags/releases, tracked checkpoints, results or immutable dataset receipts; linked weights are in an unchecksummed Drive folder. No processed-function artifact versioning, compatibility manifest, migration, rollback, provenance chain or registry is defined.
composition_rule: NFT blocks compose equivariant layers, self/cross-attention and pointwise maps; invariant prediction uses f composed with ENC, and editing applies W prime equals W plus Delta(W). INR2Array composes encoder, latent array and hypernetwork decoder. These are fixed model architectures, not an algebra or router for independently specified function artifacts.
state_or_effect_model: The paper processes static weight snapshots and may emit modified weights. Forward-pass activations are ordinary transient neural state; no persistent state, external effect, transaction, effect typing, isolation or rollback semantics is defined.
validation_regime: Theorem 3.1 and its appendix proof establish the stated minimal-equivariance property for the constructed layer class. Empirical checks cover CNN generalization prediction, INR classification, weight-space editing, ablations, compute and training limits. Reported run counts are small; the table/prose CIFAR discrepancy, absent immutable run receipts and non-executed local tests limit independent audit. Neither theorem nor experiments verify downstream semantic correctness.
equivalence_notions: Coupled hidden-unit permutations give an exact function-preserving relation for the supported layered networks. Equivariance means outputs transform consistently under the defined S_NP action, and invariance is obtained by cross-attention or invariant pooling/heads. The full group includes over-strong input/output permutations unless positional encodings are used. No equivalence relation is supplied for arbitrary architectures, checkpoints, learned behaviors, edits or implementation versions.

source_specific_acceptance_reasoning: The prior review correctly retains PARTIAL support and identifies the survey's three dimensions, its broad representation landscape and its catalog of weight generation and merging. It nevertheless needs material correction before synthesis. Its hash is false and its claimed complete anchor coverage omits the final twenty-two pages of substantive applications, benchmarks, open questions and safety analysis plus all references. The survey does not identify functions with a flat weight vector modulo permutation: it discusses structured tensors, learned latent embeddings, probe-derived behavioral representations and generated distributions, and its symmetry examples include permutations, scaling, logit translation, rotations, sign changes and head transformations. Even the stated quotient W/G is an orbit under a chosen symmetry group, not a complete decision procedure for every pair of weights that realizes the same behavior. Model-based versus model-free is the WSR representation split; WSG instead separates hypernetworks from generative models and further catalogs autoencoding, adversarial, autoregressive and iterative-denoising families. Section 4.2.3 contrasts raw averaging/interpolation with latent or distribution-aware merging and alignment; it neither defines task arithmetic as its composition rule nor supplies a formal algebra, router or preservation guarantee. The survey presents secondary synthesis and model-zoo inventory, not new experiments or a unified validator. Conversely, saying probabilistic semantics are wholly unaddressed is too broad: WSG explicitly models distributions over weights, Bayesian hypernetworks, autoregressive factorization and diffusion transitions. Those mechanisms provide stochastic-generation evidence but no probabilistic semantics, calibrated uncertainty or acceptance rule for executed functions. The resource repository is a mutable curated list with Git/CITATION identity, not an implementation or provenance registry. The corrected card remains PARTIAL and supersedes the prior record.
accepted_prior_claims: The survey organizes Weight Space Learning into Weight Space Understanding, Weight Space Representation and Weight Space Generation.
It catalogs weights, learned embeddings and generated parameters as model-level objects for analysis, retrieval, editing, synthesis and reuse.
Symmetry-aware invariance and equivariance are central structural foundations for weight-space methods.
Hypernetworks and generative models are major weight-generation families, and model merging is a surveyed technique-level use case.
The paper proposes no Function OS specification language, unified interpreter, formal composition algebra, effect system or governed versioned registry.

material_corrections.prior: A non-matching SHA-256 with ANCHOR_VERIFIED and anchor_completeness_rate 1.0 after reviewing only Sections 1-4.
material_corrections.corrected: The exact v1 SHA-256 is 542e410a7e38ddc5fde8c7a89ea4d6fa0e98daaa3f5a97ca49a065f7fe649968. Sections 5-8, benchmark tables, open questions, robustness/safety, conclusion and references were omitted from the old review list and are now fully reviewed.

material_corrections.prior: A function is a flat weight vector modulo permutation.
material_corrections.corrected: The survey treats models through raw structured parameters, symmetry-aware or graph encoders, latent embeddings, probe-based behavioral signatures and distributions. A chosen symmetry-group orbit supplies bounded structural equivalence; it is neither only permutation nor complete semantic identity.

material_corrections.prior: Weight generation is divided into model-based neural and model-free non-parametric approaches.
material_corrections.corrected: Model-based versus model-free is Section 3's representation taxonomy. Section 4 divides generation into hypernetworks and generative models, with autoencoding, adversarial, autoregressive and iterative-denoising subfamilies.

material_corrections.prior: Model merging primarily consists of averaging, task arithmetic and other weight combinations.
material_corrections.corrected: The survey contrasts conventional raw averaging/interpolation with alignment and latent/distribution-aware synthesis. It catalogs heterogeneous methods but supplies no task-arithmetic algebra, compatibility condition, routing policy or guaranteed function composition.

material_corrections.prior: The survey provides empirical benchmarks across applications.
material_corrections.corrected: It summarizes results and model zoos reported by cited works; it contributes no new benchmark experiment, reproduction, unified metric or validation service. Its own limitations say performance alone misses structural, functional and symmetry preservation.

material_corrections.prior: Probabilistic semantics are not addressed.
material_corrections.corrected: Probabilistic weight-generation mechanisms are substantively surveyed, including Bayesian hypernetworks, distributions over weights, autoregressive likelihoods and diffusion kernels. This is not probabilistic semantics or calibrated uncertainty for the resulting executed function.

material_corrections.prior: Model retrieval and merging imply a registry-like structure.
material_corrections.corrected: The paper defines retrieval over a discrete candidate set and inventories model zoos. Neither it nor the mutable companion README defines versions, artifact identities, immutable manifests, compatibility, lineage, signing, rollback or governance.

specification_language: No Function OS-style specification language is defined. Conditioning signals such as task descriptions, architecture graphs, class identities, data features or noise parameterize generators, but they are not typed behavioral contracts with preconditions, postconditions or effect clauses.
uncertainty_model: The survey catalogues Bayesian hypernetworks, latent priors, weight distributions, GAN objectives, autoregressive likelihood factorization and diffusion forward/reverse kernels. These are model-family descriptions, not a unified uncertainty interface. It provides no calibration, confidence, abstention, acceptance threshold, fuzzy semantics or uncertainty propagation from weight samples to downstream behavior.
lifecycle_and_provenance: The survey inventories public model zoos, repositories, checkpoints and model retrieval as research resources, and its companion MIT repository has Git history plus CITATION metadata. It does not define immutable dataset/checkpoint manifests, build receipts, version compatibility, ownership, lineage, evaluation attachment, migration or rollback. The paper-era companion head predates submission and the current head postdates v1, with no release/tag tying either snapshot to the paper.
composition_rule: Surveyed composition includes aligned weight interpolation, conventional averaging, latent/hyper-representation recombination, distribution-aware synthesis and modular/adaptor generation. These are method families with architecture- and symmetry-dependent failure modes; no associativity, identity, closure, semantic preservation rule, conflict resolver or router is defined.
state_or_effect_model: The paper discusses checkpoint trajectories, continual-learning task regeneration, residual updates and forecasting future weights, so temporal weight evolution is present as subject matter. It does not specify runtime state, external effects, effect typing, transactionality, isolation, rollback or safe composition of effects.
validation_regime: A secondary survey of prior empirical results, benchmark/model-zoo designs and formal symmetry concepts. It adds no experiment or independent reproduction. Open issues explicitly include absent standardized WSR metrics, nontrivial evaluation of generated models, lack of functional guarantees, safety risks and the need for rigorous benchmarks. These observations are gap evidence, not proof or empirical validation of Function OS.
equivalence_notions: Equation 1 defines invariance for a weight transformation that leaves f(theta;x) unchanged for all x; Equation 2 defines equivariance under paired input-weight and output actions. The quotient W/G records orbits of a selected symmetry group. These notions do not provide an algorithm for checking arbitrary learned networks, cross-architecture behavior, code-to-weight equivalence or version-to-version compatibility, and group orbits need not exhaust all behaviorally equivalent parameterizations.
